solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Women work bringing in everything for buffet

indicators.note: bringing in says the pair of pieces before it take the everything word between them

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work
everything means all

explanation.surface: Women at work bring in a full spread for a buffet lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' looks like a meal, but it is the verb meaning to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To buffet is to strike hard, and a wallop is a heavy blow; both work as verbs too.

clue.text: Went away and doctor put us up

parts.note: with can mean and, as in 'bread with butter'

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for us is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: us is the object form of we

explanation.surface: Someone left, and a doctor gave the family somewhere to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is not a link here: it supplies WITH.
explanation.definitionFit: To withdraw is to retreat or leave, so the past tense means departed.

clue.text: Security man's hair trigger's initially squeezed by him being upset

parts.note: locks are tresses of hair

indicators.note: squeezed by says the first letter is pressed inside the jumbled word
being upset says the letters of him are thrown into disorder
initially picks the opening letter of the word trigger's

explanation.surface: A security guard with a hair-trigger temper is cornered by someone furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being upset' scrambles HIM to MIH, and 'squeezed by' puts T inside it to give MITH.
explanation.definitionFit: A locksmith makes and fits locks, so is a tradesman in the security business.

clue.text: Love film anyone can see, Disney's Up and maybe Robin Hood

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
U is the British certificate for a film suitable for everyone

indicators.note: in a down clue, Up means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Walt Disney founded the studio

explanation.surface: A list of family films: Disney's Up and a Robin Hood picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' looks like the Pixar film title, but it signals reading WALT backwards to TLAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the classic example of a bandit living outside the law.

clue.text: On top of the world until jab administered!

indicators.note: administered suggests the letters of until and jab are dealt out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is overjoyed right up to the moment the injection is given.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on top of the world is an idiom for feeling elated and triumphant.

clue.text: Embarrassing with peacekeepers' corps primarily to blame for unrest

parts.note: UN peacekeepers are troops of the United Nations

indicators.note: primarily picks the opening letter of the word corps
unrest says the letters of to blame for are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: An awkward situation in which UN troops are mainly blamed for civil disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unrest' rearranges TO BLAME FOR into OMFORTABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An embarrassing moment leaves people ill at ease, which is this awkward feeling.

clue.text: Brewed at home and FBI agent catches us

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'

indicators.note: catches says the agent's word closes around the letters of us

parts.note: a fed is slang for a US federal agent
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cuppa brewed at home while an FBI agent catches us out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea that has infused has steeped in hot water, the same as having brewed.

clue.text: Boxer has a second alternative name

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, the famous heavyweight boxer

explanation.surface: A boxer has a second, and also goes by another name.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Ali himself was born Cassius Clay, so he really had another name.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is an assumed name used instead of one's own.

clue.text: Labelled goods in date order

indicators.note: in says the doubled letter sits inside the rearranged word
order says the letters of date are rearranged

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good, so two of them give GG

explanation.surface: Products are labelled and arranged by date in a warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges the date into TAED; 'goods' is two Gs, one for each good, not merchandise.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tagged has had a tag, a small label, attached to it.

clue.text: Understood diplomacy surrounding island

indicators.note: surrounding says the word for diplomacy goes around the letter for island

parts.note: tact is diplomacy in dealing with people

explanation.surface: An unspoken agreement reached by diplomacy over an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A tacit agreement is implied and understood without being spoken.

clue.text: Calming down by walking around, for your information

indicators.note: around says the walking word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: pacing is walking back and forth

explanation.surface: Advice that pacing the room helps settle nerves, offered as a helpful tip.
explanation.definitionFit: To pacify is to soothe someone, so the participle means soothing or settling.

clue.text: Start writing to suggest enclosure for Times perhaps?

definitions.meaning: to begin composing a letter or text
a pen is an enclosure, and the Times is a paper, so this reads as placing a pen next to a paper

explanation.walkthrough: 'enclosure' looks like something enclosed in a letter to the Times; it is a pen for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means beginning to write something down, literally bringing nib to sheet.

clue.text: Daughter's first to get amazing tan abroad

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
1ST, written with I for the numeral one, means first

indicators.note: amazing here means bewildering, so the letters of tan are confused

explanation.surface: A daughter is the first in the family to get a stunning tan on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives 1ST with the digit read as I. 'amazing' turns TAN into ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Abroad means far away in another country, so remote or far-off.

clue.text: Have to understand it's something everyone should visit

parts.note: must means have to
to see is to understand, as in 'I see'

explanation.surface: A tourist guide explains that you have to understand this attraction is essential.
explanation.definitionFit: A must-see is an attraction regarded as essential viewing for every visitor.

clue.text: English team's time is way out

parts.note: XI, Roman eleven, stands for a team such as a cricket or football side

explanation.surface: An English sports team's timing is way off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way out' reads as 'badly wrong' but means a door marked for leaving. A cricket or football side has eleven players.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is literally a way out of a building or space.

clue.text: Instrument from LP by Queen

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing vinyl record
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A musical instrument taken from an album by the band Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' looks like the rock band, but gives ER.
explanation.definitionFit: The recorder is a simple woodwind instrument often learned at school.

clue.text: Add program again and check delay

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
to stall is to delay

explanation.surface: Instructions to reload some software and check why it is lagging.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting up software once more on a computer is reloading it a second time.

clue.text: Freak out over blasted photo

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: to snap is to lose one's temper suddenly
shot means blasted, as with a gun

explanation.surface: Someone loses it over a ruined picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blasted' looks like a mild curse on the photo, but means fired upon.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quick informal photograph.

clue.text: Hang back with chap and take seat at rear of theatre

parts.note: he refers to a chap
to sit is to take a seat

indicators.note: rear of picks the final letter of the word theatre

explanation.surface: A man waits back with a friend before sitting at the back of the playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang back is to hold off or waver, unwilling to go forward.

clue.text: Rescue from beastly crossing over lake

indicators.note: crossing over says the beastly word spans the letter for lake, with it inside

parts.note: savage means beastly, wild and cruel

explanation.surface: A daring rescue from a wild animal crossing a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvage is saving goods or a vessel from loss, a kind of rescue.

clue.text: Indication Beijing is partially backtracking

indicators.note: backtracking says the hidden letters are read backwards
partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A political hint that the Chinese government is reversing a policy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign is a signal or pointer that something is the case.

clue.text: Consider supporting soldier to rehabilitate

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting puts the word for consider underneath, holding up the soldier

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier
to deem is to consider or judge

explanation.surface: A plan to back a soldier and help restore his reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: To redeem someone is to restore their good name, as rehabilitating does.

clue.text: Prince gets equal treatment on memorial stone

indicators.note: treatment says the letters of equal are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A prince is treated the same as anyone else on a commemorative stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaque is an inscribed tablet fixed to a wall to commemorate someone.

clue.text: Cover cut after infection finally penetrated day before

indicators.note: after puts the cutting word at the end of the answer
penetrated says that letter gets inside the word for the day before

parts.note: eve is the day before an event, as in Christmas Eve

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word infection

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A wound got infected and spread the day after a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penetrated' slips the last letter of infection into the day before to make ENVE; 'after' sends the cut to the end, against the clue's order.
explanation.definitionFit: To envelop is to wrap or cover something completely.

clue.text: Checks son's wearing underwear

indicators.note: wearing says the letter for son sits inside the checking word, as a body inside clothes

parts.note: to vet is to check thoroughly
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent checks what underclothes their son has on.
explanation.definitionFit: Vests are sleeveless undergarments worn beneath a shirt in British usage.

clue.text: Puts on safety restraint and stays quiet

definitions.meaning: keeps one's mouth shut, a British slang phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is British slang telling someone to shut up.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both fastening a belt and falling silent.

clue.text: Sea change, when following young person's lead that is, becomes very simple

indicators.note: following puts the word for when after the letter for young
change says the letters of sea are altered in order

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: lead picks the opening letter of the word person's

parts.note: IE, from id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A shift at sea seems simple when you follow a youngster's example.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a task so easy it needs no effort at all.

clue.text: Defeat question with a silence

parts.note: SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: Someone shuts down a query with a hush.
explanation.definitionFit: To quash a motion or rebellion is to defeat or suppress it.

clue.text: Failed to pick up his dream career

indicators.note: to career is to rush wildly, so the letters of his and dream hurtle into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone missed hearing about his dream job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a job, but is the verb for hurtling out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up can mean to catch what is said, and getting it wrong is failing to do so.

clue.text: E Zola's work has tenor that's radical

indicators.note: work suggests the letters of E Zola are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: A novel by Émile Zola features a tenor with extreme views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' looks like Zola's novel, but scrambles E ZOLA into ZEALO.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot is a fanatic, someone with extreme or radical opinions.
